stories.headline: Trump Calls Iran's Reply to Peace Plan 'Totally Unacceptable'; Brent Jumps 4% to $105

key_facts.fact: Iran sent its response to the latest US ceasefire proposal to Pakistani mediators on Sunday, May 10, saying negotiations should focus on permanently ending hostilities across the region
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has sent its response to the latest U.S. ceasefire proposal to Pakistani mediators and wants negotiations to focus on permanently ending the war, Iran's state-run media said Sunday.

key_facts.fact: President Trump called Iran's counterproposal 'totally unacceptable' Sunday hours after Tehran delivered it through Pakistani mediators
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump called Iran's response to the latest U.S. proposal to end the war 'totally unacceptable.'

key_facts.fact: Washington's 14-point plan requires Iran to end its nuclear programme for at least 12 years and open the Strait of Hormuz, while lifting decades-long sanctions; Iran demands war reparations, full sovereignty over the strait, an end to the US blockade and release of frozen assets
key_facts.excerpt: Washington floated a 14-point proposal earlier this week, which requires Iran to end its nuclear programme for at least 12 years and open the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global crude oil and gas passes. The US proposal includes lifting the decades-long sanctions.

key_facts.fact: A QatarEnergy-operated LNG carrier, al Kharaitiyat, was permitted to pass through the Strait of Hormuz Sunday and head for Pakistan's Port Qasim, the first Qatari LNG vessel through the strait since the war started February 28
key_facts.excerpt: But the QatarEnergy-operated carrier al Kharaitiyat passed safely through the strait and was heading for Pakistan's Port Qasim, according to data from shipping analytics firm Kpler, the first Qatari vessel carrying liquefied natural gas to cross the strait since the U.S. and Israel started the war on Feb. 28.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures climbed $4.16, or 4.11%, to $105.45 a barrel in Monday Asian trading; WTI rose $4.38, or 4.59%, to $99.80
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures climbed $4.16 or 4.11% to $105.45 a barrel at 0340 GMT. U.S. West Texas Intermediate was at $99.80 a barrel, up $4.38, or 4.59%.

key_facts.fact: Both Brent and WTI had recorded 6% weekly losses the prior week on hopes of an imminent deal that would reopen the strait; ING analysts now expect Brent to stay above $90 through 2026 and $80–85 into 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Last week, both contracts recorded 6% weekly losses on hopes for an imminent end to the 10-week-old conflict... They expected Brent to remain above $90 per barrel through 2026 and around $80 to $85 per barrel into 2027 as demand growth resumes and inventories are gradually rebuilt.

stories.headline: Netanyahu: War With Iran 'Not Over'; Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire Near Collapse Amid Strikes

key_facts.fact: On Sunday, May 10, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the war with Iran is 'not over,' warning Tehran still possesses enriched uranium, ballistic missile capabilities and regional proxy networks that Israel intends to dismantle
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Sunday that the war with Iran is 'not over,' warning that Tehran still possesses enriched uranium, ballistic missile capabilities and regional proxy networks that Israel intends to dismantle.

key_facts.fact: Netanyahu signaled that fighting with Hezbollah may continue after a cease-fire, with no clear end to operations against the Iran-backed militia in southern Lebanon
key_facts.excerpt: Netanyahu Says Iran War 'Not Over,' Signals Hezbollah Fighting May Continue After Cease-fire

key_facts.fact: Fresh Israeli airstrikes targeted Hezbollah positions and infrastructure used to launch attacks into northern Israel, while Hezbollah launched rocket and drone fire toward Israeli territory, raising fears the US-backed truce may collapse
key_facts.excerpt: New Israeli airstrikes and continued cross-border fire from Hezbollah are raising concerns that the US-backed ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon may be nearing collapse. Both sides accuse each other of violations and civilians are caught in the escalating conflict.

key_facts.fact: The Israel-Lebanon ceasefire took effect April 16 and was extended for three weeks by Trump; both sides have been operating in a 'gray zone' since, with Israel striking Beirut's southern suburbs for the first time since the truce earlier in the week
key_facts.excerpt: The ceasefire, brokered with heavy involvement from the United States, was intended to halt hostilities after months of tit-for-tat attacks linked to the fallout from the Gaza war. However, both sides are operating in a gray zone to avoid triggering full-scale war while signalling resolve.

key_facts.fact: Iran's response to the US ceasefire proposal explicitly included demands on Lebanon and Hormuz maritime security, with Tehran insisting any deal must cover ending the war 'in all arenas,' particularly Lebanon
key_facts.excerpt: Tehran's response focused on ending the war in all arenas, particularly Lebanon, Iranian state television reported. Additionally, the semi-official ISNA reported that it also focused on maritime 'security' in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Trump-Xi Summit Set May 14-15 in Beijing; Iran, Taiwan, AI, Nuclear Arms on Agenda

key_facts.fact: US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14 and 15, his first trip to China since 2017 and first leader-level US visit to Beijing in nearly a decade
key_facts.excerpt: Trump is scheduled to arrive in Beijing on Wednesday, ahead of talks set to take place Thursday and Friday. It will be his first trip to China since 2017.

key_facts.fact: US officials briefing reporters on May 10 said the agenda will span Iran, Taiwan, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons, with both sides weighing whether to extend a critical-minerals truce reached last October
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are set to discuss Iran, Taiwan, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons as they weigh extending a critical minerals deal, according to U.S. officials previewing Trump's two-day visit to China this week.

key_facts.fact: China is expected to announce purchases of Boeing aircraft, US agricultural goods and energy, with proposals under discussion including 25 million metric tons of soybeans annually for three years and a potential deal for 500 Boeing 737 MAX jets
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. is pushing for significant Chinese purchases of poultry, beef, and energy products, alongside a multi-year commitment to buy 25 million metric tons of soybeans annually. A centerpiece of the discussions involves Boeing, which has been in prolonged talks with Beijing for a deal potentially including 500 737 MAX jets.

key_facts.fact: Iran is a flashpoint heading into the meeting: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has urged Beijing to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while China maintains that ending the war is Washington's responsibility
key_facts.excerpt: The Iran war presents a complex diplomatic hurdle. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has urged China to join efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though Beijing maintains that ending the conflict is Washington's responsibility.

key_facts.fact: Beijing 'is working backward from our midterm elections,' meaning major economic concessions are unlikely; the two sides are expected to set up a 'Board of Trade' mechanism to expand commerce in non-sensitive sectors
key_facts.excerpt: China may not offer breakthroughs when Trump meets Xi because Beijing is 'working backward from our midterm elections'

stories.headline: Microsoft-G42 $1B Kenya Data Center Stalls After Government Won't Guarantee Payments

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported May 10 that Microsoft and Abu Dhabi-based G42's planned data center in East Africa has been delayed by disagreements with the Kenyan government over the partners' request for guaranteed annual capacity payments
key_facts.excerpt: A Microsoft data center site in East Africa has been delayed by disagreements with the Kenyan government over the company's request for guaranteed payments, Bloomberg News reported on Sunday citing people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft and G42 asked Kenya to commit to paying for a certain amount of capacity annually, but when the government couldn't meet that level the talks broke down; sources said the group may scale back the project
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft and G42 asked the Kenyan government to commit to paying for a certain amount of capacity annually, but the talks broke down when it couldn't provide the guarantees at the level Microsoft requested, the Bloomberg report said. The Bloomberg report added that the group might ultimately decide to scale back the project.

key_facts.fact: The $1 billion geothermal-powered facility was announced during President William Ruto's May 2024 Washington visit under the Biden administration, set to deliver Microsoft Azure cloud services to East Africa from a site about 100 km northwest of Nairobi
key_facts.excerpt: In May 2024, Microsoft partnered with UAE-based AI firm G42 to invest $1 billion in a data center in Kenya as part of its efforts to expand cloud-computing services in East Africa. The project was announced during Kenyan President William Ruto's state visit to Washington under the Biden administration.

key_facts.fact: Kenya's installed power capacity is about 3,000 MW; Ruto told grassroots leaders the data center would require roughly a third of that, saying 'to switch on that one data center, we would need to shut off power for half the country'
key_facts.excerpt: 'To switch on that one data center, we would need to shut off power for half the country,' he said of the project. 'That's when I knew there was a problem.'

key_facts.fact: Kenya disputed the 'stalled' framing on May 10, with Special Tech Envoy Philip Thigo saying the project remains on track and the government aims to scale generation capacity to at least 10,000 MW by 2030
key_facts.excerpt: 'President Ruto's message was clear: While the energy demands of next-generation technologies are significant, Kenya is committed to scaling up our power capacity to at least 10,000 megawatts by 2030. This will ensure projects like the Microsoft-G42 data centre can thrive,' Thigo said.

stories.headline: Cerebras Lifts IPO Price Range to $150-160 on Surging Demand, Targeting ~$4.8B Raise

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported May 10 that Cerebras Systems plans to raise the price range on its US IPO from $115–125 to $150–160 per share amid soaring investor demand for the AI inference chip maker
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: Cerebras plans to raise its IPO price range from $115 to $125 per share to $150 to $160 per share, potentially raising ~$4.8B at the top of the range

key_facts.fact: At the top of the new range Cerebras would raise roughly $4.8 billion, potentially the largest IPO globally so far in 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras inference chips aim for the biggest IPO globally so far this year Cerebras Systems is reportedly preparing to lift both the size and price of its IPO after investor demand for the AI chipmake[r] surges

key_facts.fact: Cerebras positions its wafer-scale chips as alternatives to Nvidia GPUs for AI inference workloads; the listing has drawn comparisons to recent AI-infrastructure IPOs, with skeptics warning of scaling and execution risk
key_facts.excerpt: I wouldn't touch Cerebras with a 100 foot pole. Sure, it may go up on hype sentiment in the short term, but it's far too fundamentally risky (scaling and future execution)

stories.headline: Turkey's Grand Games Raises $70M Series B Led by Balderton, Total Funding Hits $103M

key_facts.fact: Turkish mobile gaming startup Grand Games raised $70 million in a Series B round led by Balderton Capital's Growth Fund, announced May 11
key_facts.excerpt: Grand Games has secured a $70 million Series B round led by Balderton, bringing its total investment to $103 million.

key_facts.fact: Bek Ventures, Laton Ventures and angel investor Mert Gur also participated; Balderton doubled down on its initial 2025 investment in the company
key_facts.excerpt: Bek Ventures, Laton Ventures and angel investor Mert Gur also invested, while Balderton doubled down on its initial investment from last year, according to a company statement. The latest financing brings Grand Games' total funding to $103 million.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2024 by Bekir Batuhan Çelebi, Mehmet Çalım and Mustafa Fırtına, Grand Games has grown revenue nearly fivefold over the past year and reached the top two spots on the US iOS download charts with its 'Grapphen' title
key_facts.excerpt: This follows a successful year of growth for the company, which has grown its revenue nearly fivefold and reached the top two spots on the U.S. iOS download charts with its titles 'Grapphen'. Grand Games was founded in 2024 by Bekir Batuhan Çelebi, Mehmet Çalım, and Mustafa Fırtına.

key_facts.fact: The company runs an autonomous-team structure of five independent studios and will use the new capital to expand the team and launch new games globally
key_facts.excerpt: The company attributes its growth to an autonomous organizational model consisting of five independent studios. The investment aims to grow its team and introduce new games to wider audiences.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco CEO: World Has Lost ~1 Billion Barrels of Oil in Two Months of Hormuz Crisis

key_facts.fact: Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said Sunday, May 10, the world has lost about 1 billion barrels of oil over the past two months and energy markets will take time to stabilise even if flows resume
key_facts.excerpt: The world has lost about 1 billion barrels of oil over the past two months and energy markets will take time to stabilise even if flows resume, Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said on Sunday.

key_facts.fact: Two more crude tankers exited the Strait of Hormuz last week with trackers switched off to avoid Iranian attacks, Kpler shipping data showed, reflecting a growing workaround to keep Middle East exports moving
key_facts.excerpt: Another two tankers carrying crude exited the Strait of Hormuz last week with trackers switched off to avoid Iranian attacks, Kpler shipping data showed, underscoring a rising trend to sustain Middle East oil exports.

key_facts.fact: Brent's prompt spread widened to nearly $4 a barrel in backwardation Monday morning, a bullish structure signalling strong demand for immediate supplies; more than 4,000 lots of Brent's July contract traded in the first five minutes
key_facts.excerpt: More than 4,000 lots of Brent's July contract changed hands in the first five minutes of trading, far above recent averages. Brent's prompt spread widened to nearly $4 a barrel in backwardation, a bullish structure that signals strong demand for immediate supplies.

key_facts.fact: A Goldman Sachs survey of clients found most respondents expect Hormuz disruptions to continue well into the second half of 2026
key_facts.excerpt: A survey by Goldman Sachs Group found that most respondents expect disruptions in Hormuz to continue well into the second half of the year.
